territorial_scope.description: Applies to political communications covered by Wisconsin statute s. 11.1303, a state-level provision.

evidence.quote: Every audio communication otherwise described in sub. (2) (a) or (b)

summary.short: Wisconsin amends its statute s. 11.1303 to require that audio and video political communications containing AI-generated synthetic media carry specified 'generated by AI' labels, with a forfeiture of up to $1,000 per intentional violation. It applies to communications created on the subsection's effective date.
summary.long: The Act amends Wisconsin statute s. 11.1303 by creating subsection (2m) on synthetic media in political communications. 'Synthetic media' means audio or video content substantially produced in whole or in part by generative artificial intelligence. The labelling duties cover communications described in s. 11.1303(2)(a) or (b) that contain express advocacy, issue advocacy, or support or opposition to a referendum. Audio communications must include the words 'Contains content generated by AI.' at the beginning and at the end. Video communications must display, throughout each portion containing synthetic media, readable text stating one of three specified phrases depending on whether the synthetic media is video, audio or both. The commission may promulgate implementing rules, which may include limited exceptions. Compliance does not exempt a person from civil or criminal liability, including under s. 12.05. Intentional violations of the labelling duties carry a forfeiture of up to $1,000 per violation, enforced under s. 11.1400(5). Broadcasters and other hosts or carriers are not liable unless they are the committee responsible for the communication, and the subsection does not alter rights under 47 USC 230. Initial applicability covers communications created on the subsection's effective date.

relations.note: Section 1 amends the title of s. 11.1303; Section 2 creates new sub. (2m) of the same section.

notes: The document reproduces only the amended title and the new sub. (2m) (Sections 1-3). Sub. (2)(a) and (b), which the new paragraphs cross-refer to for the covered communications, are not reproduced, so the scope cannot be fully identified from this text. The act year, number and bill (2023 Wisconsin Act 123, Assembly Bill 664) come from registry metadata, not the document. The text gives no effective date; Section 3(1) applies the act to communications created on the effective date of the subsection, which is not stated. The commission in par. (d) is not named in the act. The terms generative artificial intelligence and express advocacy are not defined in the text. The audio label in par. (b) and the video labels in par. (c) use different wording, as written. Section 3 is the only applicability provision.

thresholds.note: The only numeric amount in the text is the forfeiture maximum of $1,000 per violation in Sec. 2 (2m)(f), which is a penalty maximum and is therefore coded under enforcement, not thresholds. The text contains no numeric scope, eligibility, exemption, obligation-tier or prohibition cutoffs. The effective date is tied to the act's effective date without a number.
